name: Kompang
description: The Kompang is the most popular traditional drum in Malaysia, widely used in social gatherings like weddings and national ceremonies.
history: Believed to have Arabic origins, it was brought to the Malay Archipelago by traders during the Malacca Sultanate. It is a frame drum made of a circular wooden frame and a goat-hide head.

name: Serunai
description: The Serunai is a double-reed woodwind instrument known for its high-pitched, nasal tone, often leading the melody in Wayang Kulit performances.
history: Related to the North Indian 'shehnai', it features a wooden body and a flared bell. It requires 'circular breathing' techniques to play continuous haunting melodies.

name: Sape
description: Often called the 'Boat Lute', the Sape is a traditional lute of the Orang Ulu community, known for its soothing, dream-like sounds.
history: Traditionally carved from a single block of adau wood, it was originally used by shamans in healing rituals. Modern Sapes now feature 3 to 5 strings and are used for social dances.
